        COME NOW the City of Las Cruces (the “City” or “CLC”) and Doña Ana County (the

“County” or “DAC”), by and through their undersigned attorneys, and pro se intervenors Stephen

Fischmann and Philip B. Simpson (collectively, the “Joint Parties”) and, pursuant to 1.2.2.37

NMAC, move the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission (the “NMPRC” or “Commission”)

for an order clarifying and, as appropriate, reconsidering several deeply intertwined issues arising

from the Order Extending Suspension Period for Advice Notice No. 317 (“Suspension Order”),

issued on August 28, 2026 in Docket Nos. 25-00082-UT and 26-0000062 and the Order

Establishing Revised Procedural Order and Addressing Outstanding Motions (“Revised

Procedural Order”) issued on August 27, 2026 in Docket No. 25-00082-UT; as well as the Sua

Sponte Order Vacating Procedural Schedule, Tolling Pending Deadlines, and Requiring the Filing

of an Amended Application (“Sua Sponte Order”) issued on July 16, 2026 in Docket No. 25-

00082-UT; El Paso Electric Company’s (“EPE” or “Company”) Amended Application for

Revision of Retail Rates (“Amended Application”) package filed on August 6, 2026 in Docket No.

25-00082-UT; and Staff’s Completeness Report filed on August 13, 2026 in Docket No. 25-00082-

UT, which gave rise to the Revised Procedural Order and the Suspension Order.

       Specifically, the Joint Parties request clarification regarding the extent to which the

Revised Procedural Order has ruled definitely upon the procedural and substantive completeness

of EPE’s Amended Application; the need for a new or amended advice notice to reflect the

proposed rates set out in EPE’s Amended Application; and the expected content of the public

notice ordered in that Revised Procedural Order.

       The Joint Parties request clarification on whether the Suspension Order implicitly rules that

there is no need for a new or amended advice notice; whether the Suspension Order relates to the

retail rates for EPE’s customers proposed in EPE’s original Application for Revision of Retail

Electric Rates filed on March 27, 2026 in Docket No. 25-00082-UT and EPE’s Advice Notice No.

                                                 1
 317 filed on March 27, 2026 in Docket No. 26-0000062 or to the rates proposed in EPE’s Amended

Application; and whether the Suspension Order is intended to serve as a recommended decision or

a certified question to the Commission for an order extending by two months the suspension period

established by the Commission’s Order Suspending Advice Notice No. 317 issued in Docket Nos.

25-00082-UT and 26-0000062 on April 24, 2026. The Joint Parties believe that regardless of

whether EPE submits a new advice notice—which it has not included in its Amended

Application—by law the suspension period commences when the utility’s application is complete.

       As grounds for this motion, the Joint Parties state:

I.     RELEVANT PROCEDURAL HISTORY

       1.      EPE filed its Application for Revision of Retail Electric Rates (“Application”) on

March 27, 2026. See Docket No. 25-00082-UT, EPE’s Application for Revision of Retail Electric

Rates (Mar. 27, 2026). EPE filed Advice Notice No. 317 on the same date in Docket No. 26-

0000062.

       2.      On April 15, 2026, EPE filed a Notice of Errata and Filing of Replacement Exhibits.

See Docket No. 25-00082-UT, Notice of Errata and Filing of Replacement Exhibits (Apr. 15,

2026) (“First Errata Notice”).

       3.      On April 24, 2026, the Commission issued an Order Suspending Advice Notice No.

317, in which it ruled that EPE’s Application was deemed complete as of April 15, 2026, and that

the statutory period for suspension of the Company’s proposed rates should begin 30 days

thereafter and continue for an initial period of nine months. See Docket Nos. 25-00082-UT and

26-0000062, Order Suspending Advice Notice No. 317 ¶¶ 15-18 (signed on Apr. 23, 2026, and

filed on Apr. 24, 2026) (“Order Suspending Advice Notice No. 317”).

       4.      Shortly thereafter, the Hearing Examiners issued a Procedural Order that set the

procedural schedule based on the Commission-authorized suspension period and ordered public

                                                 2
 notice in accordance with Advice Notice No. 317. See Docket No. 25-00082-UT, Procedural

Order (Apr. 27, 2026) (“First Procedural Order”).

       5.      On July 7, 2026, EPE filed its Second Notice of Errata and Filing of Replacement

Exhibits. See Docket No. 25-00082-UT, EPE’s Second Notice of Errata and Filing of Replacement

Exhibits (“Second Errata Notice”).

       6.      On July 16, 2026, Hearing Examiner Barrett issued an order that required EPE to

file “one integrated and comprehensive Amended Application that supersedes the original

Application, the First Errata Notice, the Second Errata Notice, and all prior replacement or

supplemental versions of affected documents.” Sua Sponte Order Vacating Procedural Schedule,

Tolling Pending Deadlines, and Requiring the Filing of an Amended Application ¶ E (“Sua Sponte

Order”). That order required Staff to file a “Completeness Report” stating whether the Amended

Application and supporting materials are “sufficiently complete, coherent, internally consistent,

and technically usable to permit the proceeding to continue.” Id. ¶ F. Staff was ordered to consider

a number of factors, including whether EPE had adequately supplemented affected discovery

responses. See id. ¶ G; cf. id. ¶ G(9) (supplemental discovery).

       7.      At the time that the Sua Sponte Order was issued, three motions were pending in

Docket No. 25-00082-UT: the City’s Verified Motion to Dismiss EPE’s Application for Revision

of Retail Rates, filed on June 30, 2026 (“Motion to Dismiss”); the City’s Motion for an Order

Compelling EPE to Provide Responses to Discovery Requests and Tolling the Procedural Order’s

Deadlines for Intervenor and Staff Direct Testimony and Rebuttal Testimony, filed on July 2, 2026

(“Motion to Compel”); and the Expedited Joint Objection and Motion for an Order Rejecting

EPE’s Second Notice of Errata and Staying the Procedural Schedule Pending the Company’s

Compliance with NMPRC Rule 1.2.2.10(G) NMAC, filed on July 10, 2026, by the City, the

County, the New Mexico Department of Justice (“NMDOJ”), and pro se intervenors Dwight

                                                 3
 Eggers, Stephen Fischmann, and Philip B. Simpson (“Motion on Second Errata Notice”). The Sua

Sponte Order reserved ruling on those pending motions. See Sua Sponte Order ¶¶ J(1), J(2).

       8.      On August 3, 2026, NMPRC Utility Division Staff (“Staff”) filed a motion asking

for clarification of the Sua Sponte Order, including its duty to review supplemental discovery

responses. NMPRC Case No. 25-00082-UT, Motion to Clarify Sua Sponte Order (Aug. 3, 2026).

       9.      The following day, Hearing Examiners Barrett and Rossi issued an order clarifying

that Staff was “not to provide any advice or commentary on whether EPE’s substantive requests

are reasonable, lawful, or supported by the weight of the evidence.” Docket No. 25-00082-UT,

Order Clarifying Sua Sponte Order ¶ 1(a) (Aug. 4, 2026). That order also relieved Staff of the

obligation to consider whether EPE had adequately supplemented its discovery responses in

conjunction with the filing of an amended application. See id. ¶ 2(a).

       10.     Pursuant to the Sua Sponte Order, EPE filed its Amended Application on August

6, 2026.

       11.     EPE’s Amended Application did not include a revised Advice Notice No. 317 or a

new advice notice. See Amended Application ¶ 3(d) n.4. EPE’s Amended Application included

a form of “Notice to EPE Customers” that appears to be identical to that authorized by the

Commission in its Procedural Order issued on April 27, 2026. Compare Amended Application at

Ex. C, Notice to EPE Customers, with Procedural Order, Attachment A.

       12.     The amended Direct Testimony of EPE witness George Novela includes the

following question and answer:

       Q18. WHAT IS EPE’S POSITION ON WHETHER A NEW ADVICE
            NOTICE IS REQUIRED?
         E. EPE is not requesting to file a new advice notice with the proposed rates in
            the Amended Filing. The change in the Amended Filing is not material: it
            amounts to only 0.04% of the originally filed revenue requirement. At any
            rate, EPE accepts that the Commission cannot order rates higher than what
            were publicly noticed in Advice Notice No. 317.

                                                4
 Amended Application, [Amended] Direct Testimony of George Novela (“Novela Direct”) at

12:15-21.

       13.     EPE’s Amended Application offers a different rationale for not filing a new advice

notice that reflects “the proposed rates in the Amended Filing,” as Mr. Novela described. See id.

at 12:17-18. Quoting the language of the Sua Sponte Order that provided that “the effect of the

Amended Application upon the applicable statutory period, including its proposed effective date

and whether a revised advice notice is required, is reserved pending the Amended Application and

an opportunity for the parties to state their positions,” the Company concluded that it was not to

file a revised advice notice until ordered to do so by the Commission. Amended Application §§

II ¶ 3(d) n.3, ¶ 7 (quoting Sua Sponte Order ¶ 33).

       14.     On August 7, 2026, EPE filed objections to the Sua Sponte Order. See Docket No.

25-00082-UT, EPE’s Objections to Sua Sponte Order.

       15.     Pursuant to the Sua Sponte Order, Staff filed a report on August 13, 2026,

expressing its opinion that EPE’s Amended Application was sufficiently complete to allow this

matter to proceed. See Docket No. 25-00082-UT, Completeness Report at 7 (Aug. 13, 2026).

       16.     Staff’s Completeness Report addressed EPE’s failure to submit a new advice notice

and, based on the amended direct testimony of EPE witness George Novela, concluded that EPE

is “requesting approval of the noticed rates and revenue requirement included in Advice Notice

No. 317.” Id. ¶ 11.

       17.     Pursuant to the Sua Sponte Order, the intervenors were not given an opportunity to

provide their positions regarding the completeness of EPE’s Amended Application or to raise any

other objections that they might have to EPE’s Amended Application or Staff’s Completeness

Report, including ones concerning the applicable statutory suspension period, whether a revised

advice notice is required, EPE’s decision not to file a new or amended advice notice, and public

                                                 5
 notice. See Sua Sponte Order, passim; but cf. id. ¶ 33 (reserving at least questions around the

statutory suspension period and whether a revised advice notice is needed until the parties have an

opportunity to state their positions).

       18.     Following a scheduling conference held on August 25, 2026, Hearing Examiners

Gedko and Rossi issued the Order Establishing Revised Procedural Order and Addressing

Outstanding Motions (“Revised Procedural Order”) in Case No. 25-00082-UT on August 27, 2026.

Paragraph 5 of that order states that “Staff, having reviewed EPE’s Amended Application, has

opined that the Amended Application is sufficiently complete to allow this matter to proceed. The

Hearing Examiners agree.” Revised Procedural Order ¶ 5.

       19.     On August 28, 2026, Hearing Examiners Rossi and Gedko issued the Order

Extending Suspension Period for Advice Notice No. 317 in Docket Nos. 25-00082-UT and 26-

00000082 (“Suspension Order”), which contains an ordering paragraph stating that “[t]he

proposed rates filed by EPE in Advice Notice No. 317 are suspended for an additional two months,

until April 15, 2027.” Docket No. 25-00082-UT, Order ¶ A (emphasis in original).

II.    REQUESTS FOR CLARIFICATION AND RECONSIDERATION OF THE
       REVISED PROCEDURAL ORDER AND THE SUSPENSION ORDER

        A.     Suspension Period

       20.     NMSA 1978, Section 62-8-7(C) of the Public Utility Act provides that:

       Whenever there is filed with the commission by any public utility a complete
       application as prescribed by commission rule proposing new rates, the
       commission may, upon complaint or upon its own initiative, except as otherwise
       provided by law, upon reasonable notice, enter upon a hearing concerning the
       reasonableness of the proposed rates. If the commission determines a hearing is
       necessary, it shall suspend the operation of the proposed rates before they become
       effective but not for a longer initial period than nine months beyond the time
       when the rates would otherwise go into effect, unless the commission finds that
       a longer time will be required, in which case the commission may extend the
       period for an additional three months. The commission shall hear and decide cases
       with reasonable promptness. The commission shall adopt rules identifying criteria
       for various rate and tariff filings to be eligible for suspension periods shorter than

                                                 6
        what is allowed by this subsection and to be eligible for summary approval without
       hearing.

NMSA 1978, § 62-8-7(C) (emphasis added.)

       21.    The Commission’s rule on utility’s schedules of rates rules and forms, 17.1.210

NMAC, provides that:

       Incomplete Filings: Filed Rates, Rules, or Forms which do not conform to the
       requirements specified in NMPSC Rule 210 [17.1.210 NMAC] shall not be
       determined complete until all requirements are met. In the event such filings are
       found to be incomplete, the Commission shall advise the filing utility of the
       deficiency of the filing within thirty (30) days of receipt and will hold the Rates,
       Rules, or Forms for a reasonable time until the additional information required or
       necessary corrections have been provided. All applications for a change in rates
       will be considered incomplete unless accompanied by an Advice Notice, direct
       testimony, exhibits, and appropriate filing fee as required by NMPSC Rules
       210.17 and 210.13 [Subsections F and B of 17.1.210.11 NMAC]. No statutory
       deadline shall begin to be computed until the filing has been determined complete
       after notification to the utility of any deficiencies.

17.1.210.11(F) NMAC (emphasis added).

       22.    That same Rule 17.1.210 NMAC provides that:

       Completed Filings: Submitted incomplete Rates, Rules, or Forms shall be deemed
       to have been completed and acceptable when all required information and
       necessary corrections have been received by the Commission.

17.1.210.11(G) NMAC (emphasis added).

       23.    The Public Utility Act and Rule 17.1.210.11 NMAC therefore establish that the

statutory suspension period commences either when the utility makes a complete filing or when

the Commission determines that the application for new rates is complete. Earlier in this

proceeding, the Commission applied the former interpretation, consistent with NMSA Section 62-

8-7(C) and Rule 17.120.11(F) NMAC. It concluded that EPE’s original Application was deemed

complete upon filing of the First Errata Notice on April 15, 2026; the 30-day notice period under

Section NMSA 1978, Section 62-8-7(B) would be deemed to have commenced on April 15, 2026;

and the nine-month statutory suspension period of Section 62-8-7(C) would be suspended

                                                7
 “beginning 30 days after the Commission was properly notified of the proposed rate changes and

the Date EPE’s Application was considered complete, which falls on May 15, 2026.” Order

Suspending Advice Notice No. 317, ¶ 21; see also id. ¶¶ 11-16, 18, 19, A.

       24.     EPE’s decision not to file a new advice notice and its reasons for not filing a new

advice notice should not enable the Company to circumvent the operation of the statute and the

rules. Indeed, the Commission might well have found that the Amended Application was

incomplete as filed on August 6, 2026, because Rule 17.1.210.11(F) NMAC expressly states that

“[a]ll applications for a change in rates will be considered incomplete unless accompanied by an

Advice Notice….”

       25.     Perhaps the Revised Procedural Order reflects the Hearing Examiners’ conclusion

to adopt Staff’s interpretation that the absence of a new advice notice and Mr. Novela’s testimony

indicate that EPE is “requesting approved of the noticed rates and revenue requirement included

in Advice Notice No. 317.” Compare Revised Procedural Order ¶ 5 with Completeness Report,

¶¶ 11(A) & pp.7-8. Perhaps the Revised Procedural Order is premised on EPE’s interpretation of

the Sua Sponte Order in its Amended Application, although the Revised Procedural Order does

not refer to Paragraph 33 of that or to EPE’s Amended Application. See Amended Application §§

II ¶ 3(d) n.3, ¶ 7 (quoting Sua Sponte Order ¶ 33); see also supra ¶ 13; infra ¶ 58; Revised

Procedural Order, passim. The Revised Procedural Order and the Suspension Order do not reveal

the reasoning behind their rulings.

       26.     Commission precedent from dockets other than this case reaffirm such an analysis.

The only other recent case in which a revised application was ordered by the Commission in a

general rate case without assent by the utility was Case No. 21-00318-UT. Although that case

involved a rural electric cooperative’s rate application under NMSA 1978, Section 62-8-7(H) and

Rule 17.9.540 NMAC, once the prerequisites for review of a cooperative’s proposed change in

                                                8
 rates are established, the tariff suspension provisions of NMSA 1978, Section 62-8-7(C) apply.

See NMSA 1978, § 62-8-7(H).

       27.     In Case No. 21-00318-UT, the Commission suspended Jemez Mountains Electric

Cooperative, Inc.’s (“JMEC”) rates filed under Advice Notice No. 116 on December 30, 2021,

before they would have taken effect on January 29, 2022, under NMSA 1978, Section 62-8-7(B)

and Rule 17.2.210.10(D) NMAC. See NMPRC Case No. 21-00318-UT, Order Suspending

Proposed Rates and Requiring Responses ¶¶ 1, 12, A (Jan. 26, 2022). After receiving comments

from Staff and a motion from JMEC, the Commission denied JMEC’s motion for a variance to

use a 2019 base period and ordered JMEC to file an updated cost of service study that complied

with applicable NMPRC rules and utilized the most recent possible 12-month period. See NMPRC

Case No. 21-00318-UT, Order Tolling Suspension Period and Requiring Filing of Amended

Application with Updated Cost of Service Study and Requiring Staff to File Determination and

Order for Responses and Replies to NEE’s Motion to Intervene ¶¶ B, C (Feb. 23, 2022). In doing

so, the Commission tolled the suspension period for JMEC’s proposed rates pending JMEC’s filing

of an amended application. See id. ¶ A. Nineteen days after JMEC filed an amended rate

application, the Commission issued an order in which it “lifted” its previously ordered tolling of

the suspension period and suspended JMEC’s advice notice for a period of nine months effective

the date of its order. See NMPRC Case No. 21-000318-UT, Order Appointing Hearing Examiner

and Lift the Tolling of the Suspension Period, ¶ A (June 29, 2022); see also id. ¶¶ 1, 3, 14. The

filing of a sufficiently complete amended application—not the date upon which JMEC’s original

application was filed—dictated the suspension period for a hearing on the amended application

and revised rates. See id.

       28. Moreover, in Case No. 21-00318-UT, JMEC’s amended application included an

amended Advice Notice No. 116 and other documents required of cooperative, but not testimony

                                                9
 and exhibits. See id. ¶¶ 9, 10; see also NMPRC Case No. 21-00318-UT, Amended Application of

JMEC for Approval of General Rate Adjustment ¶ 29 & Advice Notice No. 116 (June 10, 2022).

Even in a situation in which the filing of testimony and exhibits was not required, the cooperative

filed a revised advice notice to reflect the changes arising from its cost of service study. See id.

       29.     Clarification of the reasons why the Commission has accepted EPE’s Amended

Application without a new advice notice as being complete might be helpful in determining when

the statutory suspension period begins to run. However, the Public Utility Act, Rule 17.1.210

NMAC, the Commission’s Order Suspending Advice Notice No. 317, and the orders in Case No.

21-00318-UT all stand for the proposition that the suspension period for a hearing on EPE’s

Amended Application should begin no earlier than 30 days after the Amended Application was

filed by EPE, or on September 5, 2026.

       30.     The Joint Parties therefore respectfully request reconsideration of the Suspension

Order and, if appropriate, the Revised Procedural Order. The Suspension Order asserts that the

suspension of the proposed rates filed by EPE in Advice Notice No. 317 are suspended for an

additional two months, under April 15, 2027. See Suspension Order ¶¶ 10, A. Unless and until

the Commission clarifies whether EPE’s Amended Application seeks approval of the proposed

rates filed on March 17, 2026, under Advice Notice No. 317 and that those originally filed rates

are the subject of the hearing in this matter—despite the Company’s inclusion of revised tariffs in

both Exhibit GN-4 to Mr. Novela’s amended Direct Testimony and in Workpaper O.4 of its

amended Application, as well as in Exhibits MC-9 and MC-10 of EPE witness Manuel Carrasco’s

amended Direct Testimony and the Company’s support of those revised tariffs throughout its

Amended Application—the suspension period should commence with the filing (or acceptance)

of EPE’s Amended Application setting forth those rates. See infra ¶¶ 53, 55-59.



                                                 10
        31.       The Joint Parties also request reconsideration of the Suspension Order insofar as it

appears to make a final determination on extension for an additional two months of a statutory

suspension period determined by the Commission itself to be nine months. See Suspension Order,

¶¶ 3, 8-10, A.

       32.       The order issued by Hearing Examiners Rossi and Gedko on August 28, 2026,

contains an ordering paragraph that states that “[t]he proposed rates filed by EPE in Advice Notice

No. 317 are suspended for an additional two months, until April 15, 2027.” Suspension Order ¶

A (emphasis in original).

       33.       NMSA 1978, Section 62-8-7(C) authorizes the Commission to suspend the

operation of proposed rates for an initial period not longer than nine months from the time when

the rates would otherwise go into effect, unless the Commission determines that a longer time will

be required, in which case the Commission may extend the period for an additional three months.

       34.       The power to suspend proposed rates and to extend previously ordered suspension

periods traditionally has rested with the Commission itself.

       35.       This power to suspend proposed rates has been delegated by the Commission to a

single commissioner in extraordinary situations. Rule 1.2.2.30(B)(4) NMAC provides that “in the

absence of a quorum and when prompt action is necessary to avoid the effectiveness of a rate

increases for customers of utilities or telecommunications providers by operation of law, [the

chairman of the commission or any other commissioner may issue orders] suspending the

operation of a rate increase request, provided that such procedural order is consistent with law and

does not involve the final determination of the proceeding.”

       36.       The revisions to the Commission’s rules of procedure that were adopted recently in

the Final Order in NMPRC Docket No. 23-00119-UT, but which have not yet been published in

the New Mexico Register and have not yet taken effect, would remove the current conditions

                                                  11
 precedent of the absence of a quorum and the need for prompt action. See NMPRC Docket No.

23-00119-UT, Final Order at Exhibit A, 1.2.2.30(B)(4) NMAC (Aug. 27, 2026). The amended

rule would delegate authority to the chairperson or a single commissioner the authority to

“suspend[ ] the operation of an advice notice, providing that such procedural order is consistent

with law and does not involve the final determination of the proceeding.” Id. 3.

        37.     The power to suspend rates or to extend suspension periods pursuant to NMSA

1978, Section 62-8-7(C) has not been delegated to presiding officers in the Commission’s current

rules of procedure. See 1.2.2.29(C), (D) NMAC.

        38.     The Sua Sponte Order recognized that the Commission, and not the Hearing

Examiners, have the authority to extend the statutory suspension period. See Sua Sponte Order ¶

J; see also id. at ¶¶ 29, 32, 33, D.

        39.     The pending amendments to the Commission’s rules of procedure do not give

presiding officers the power to suspend the operation of an advice notice or to extend the

suspension period previously authorized by the Commission. See NMPRC Docket No. 23-00119-

UT, Final Order at Exhibit A, at 1.2.2.29(C), (D) NMAC.

        40.     To the contrary, the amendments explicitly would impose upon presiding officers

the duty to issue a recommended decision “as soon as practicable before the termination of any

suspension period, review period, or other deadline imposed by or upon the commission.” See id.

at 1.2.2.29(D)(2) NMAC.

        41.     The Public Regulation Commission Act authorizes the Commission to appoint a

hearing examiner to preside over any matter before the Commission and requires the hearing

examiner to provide a written recommendation including findings of fact and conclusions of law.

See NMSA 1978, §§ 62-19-20(A), (B). That Act allows the Commissions to “delegate authority

as it deems necessary and appropriate, clearly delineating such delegated authority and any

                                               12
 limitations.” See NMSA 1978, § 62-19-9(B)(1). The Commission’s rules of procedure, 1.2.2.2

NMAC, do not delegate the authority to suspend rates or to extend suspension periods to hearing

examiners, and the Joint Parties are not aware of any other clear delegation of that statutory power.

       42.     The Joint Parties are aware of only one general rate case in which a hearing

examiner has extended a statutory suspension period, and that case involved an extension that the

applicant utility did not oppose. See NMPRC Docket No. 25-00079-UT, Order Partially Granting

Joint Motion to Extend Rate Suspension Period, ¶¶ 1, 5-9, A, B (Mar. 12, 2026). Because the

utility expressly did not oppose that extension of the suspension period, the question of the hearing

examiners’ legal authority to extend the suspension period may not arise in that still-pending

proceeding.

       43.     On the other hand, the Commission long has been cognizant of the limits upon its

own power, and the power of its hearing examiners, to suspend the operation of advice notices and

to extend previously approved suspension periods. Perhaps the most significant, and surely the

most controversial, issue addressed in the rulemaking proceeding in Docket No. 23-00119-UT was

the policy instituted by hearing examiners of “tolling” the statutory suspension period to facilitate
